title: Cabled triangle shawl
subtitle: A top-down DK triangle with a 4-stitch cable panel running down the spine.
excerpt: A top-down triangular shawl in DK wool with a single 4-stitch front cable panel running down the centre-back spine, flanked by garter stitch wings. Wingspan 150 cm, centre-back depth 70 cm when blocked. About 350 g of DK yarn. The cable travels every 4 rows.
sourceNotes: Top-down triangle construction follows Elizabeth Zimmermann, Knitting Without Tears (1971). The 4-stitch front cable panel in the centre of a shawl spine is a modern structural interpretation; Barbara Walker, A Treasury of Knitting Patterns (1968), §Cables, documents the C4F stitch.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 44 rows = 10 × 10 cm in garter stitch on 4 mm needles, blocked.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Wingspan 150 cm. Centre-back depth 70 cm. Blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: Slip 2 stitches to a cable needle and hold at the front of the work. Knit the next 2 stitches, then knit the 2 stitches from the cable needle. Creates a 4-stitch cable crossing that leans to the left.
A small strip of garter stitch worked on a few stitches, rotated and picked up to form the centre-back starting point of a top-down triangle shawl.

content.text: A top-down DK triangle shawl with one C4F cable panel running down the centre-back spine. The wings are plain garter. Wingspan 150 cm, depth 70 cm.

Top-down construction suits a spine cable well: the cable starts at three stitches and travels straight down the centre, uninterrupted, from start to cast-off edge. The wings are plain garter, so the cable panel stands out clearly as the focus of the design. The
C4F
crosses every 4 rows. Budget about 350 g (770 m / 840 yards) of DK wool.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: About 350 g (770 m / 840 yards) of DK-weight yarn

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) circular needle, 80 cm or longer

items.name: Cable needle
items.qty: 1 short cable needle for the C4F

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 4 (two at wing increase points, two to mark the 4-stitch cable panel)

content.text: Gauge

22 stitches and 44 rows to 10 cm over garter stitch on 4 mm needles, blocked. The cable panel draws in slightly: at gauge the 4-stitch spine cable measures about 1.5 cm wide, which does not affect the overall wingspan calculation significantly. If your blocked garter gauge is 24 stitches per 10 cm, the finished wingspan will be about 138 cm rather than 150 cm at the same row count.
Stitches used

items.name: C4F
items.qty: cable 4 front: slip 2 sts to cable needle, hold front, k2, k2 from cable needle

content.text: Pattern
Garter tab
Work the
garter tab

: 3 sts on waste yarn, 6 garter rows, switch to main yarn, pick up 9 sts total across tab edges. Knit 1 WS row. Place cable markers around the central 4 stitches (stitches 3 to 6 of the 9-stitch starting row). Place increase markers after st 1 and before st 9 (the edge stitches).
Increase and cable section
RS row (cable round): k1, yo, k to cable marker, SM, C4F, SM, k to 1 st before end marker, yo, k1. (increases at both ends; C4F at spine)
RS row (plain round, rows 2 and 4 of cable cycle): k1, yo, k to spine marker, SM, k4, SM, k to last st, yo, k1.
WS rows: k all sts (garter). The spine cable stitches are also knitted on WS rows.

Work the C4F on every 4th RS row (rows 1, 5, 9, 13 etc. of the RS sequence). Continue until wingspan reaches 150 cm. At gauge this is approximately 165 RS increase rows, giving 9 + (4 × 165) = 669 stitches.
Stitch count check-ins
After 40 RS rows: 9 + 160 = 169 stitches. The cable should show 10 distinct left-leaning crossings at this point.
After 100 RS rows: 9 + 400 = 409 stitches. Wingspan approximately 95 cm.
Bind off
Work Jeny's surprisingly stretchy bind-off after completing a plain RS row (not a cable row). A standard bind-off pulls the top edge in and fights blocking across 150 cm of wingspan.
Common faults

Cable cable needle dropped: the 2 stitches on the cable needle unravelled while the body stitches were worked. Park the cable needle in the front of the fabric with the stitches pointing away from you, and hold it lightly against the work with a finger while knitting the 2 body stitches.

Cable crossing on the wrong row: the C4F was worked one RS row early or late. The cable crossings should be spaced exactly 4 RS rows apart. If the spacing is inconsistent the cable will look twisted in places.

Wing stitches pulled towards the spine: the cable tension is tighter than the garter tension. Work the cable itself slightly looser than feels natural. The cable needle method (rather than cable-without-needle) is recommended here for better tension control.
Blocking

Soak in cool water, press out in towels, pin to wingspan 150 cm and depth 70 cm. Pin the side edges straight. The cable panel will remain raised above the garter wings after blocking: this is characteristic and correct. Do not over-pin the spine cable; the raised texture is the design.
Care
Hand wash in cool water, lay flat to dry. The cable spine will soften slightly after washing. Re-block lightly to restore the wings to their pinned dimensions.
What to try next

Replace the single C4F panel with three parallel cable panels spaced across each wing for a more heavily cabled surface. Alternatively, replace the garter wings with a simple lace repeat to create a lace-and-cable shawl.
